records.title: Water stands in a pit or bed for days
records.summary: Water stands in a pit or bed for days: likely the hard layer below stops water draining
instructions: Stop sending runoff into that pit or bed.
Raise the rooting area: build the bed higher or fill the pit above ground level.
Cut an overflow notch to a safe, stable place (not automatically into another planting pit).
Move the next sowing off the lowest ground.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
records.symptom: Water stands in a pit or bed for days
likely_causes: The hard layer below stops water draining
The pit sits in a low spot that collects runoff
actions: Stop sending runoff into that pit or bed.
Raise the rooting area: build the bed higher or fill the pit above ground level.
Cut an overflow notch to a safe, stable place (not automatically into another planting pit).
Move the next sowing off the lowest ground.

records.title: Bed or pit walls washed out
records.summary: Bed or pit walls washed out: likely weak border with small stones
instructions: Rebuild with bigger stones at the base and smaller ones packed behind.
Add a stone line uphill to slow the water.
Mulch the surface and add an overflow notch.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
records.symptom: Bed or pit walls washed out
likely_causes: Weak border with small stones
No stone line uphill to slow runoff
actions: Rebuild with bigger stones at the base and smaller ones packed behind.
Add a stone line uphill to slow the water.
Mulch the surface and add an overflow notch.

records.title: Stone line undercut or burst
records.summary: Stone line undercut or burst: likely the line is not level, so water runs along it to a low point
instructions: Re-lay it level across the slope with big stones at the base.
Pack soil and small stones on the uphill side.
Leave a stone-lined spill gap at one end that leads to safe ground.
Keep it low; raise it only after watching rains.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
likely_causes: The line is not level, so water runs along it to a low point
The line is too high with no spill point
actions: Re-lay it level across the slope with big stones at the base.
Pack soil and small stones on the uphill side.
Leave a stone-lined spill gap at one end that leads to safe ground.
Keep it low; raise it only after watching rains.

records.title: Seeds did not come up
records.summary: Seeds did not come up: likely a false start: one shower then a dry gap
instructions: Run the seed sprout test on the remaining seed.
Re-sow shallower after the next soaking rain.
Cover sown spots lightly with mulch once seedlings show, and scare birds.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
likely_causes: A false start: one shower then a dry gap
Old or dead seed
Sown too deep
Birds or ants took the seed
actions: Run the seed sprout test on the remaining seed.
Re-sow shallower after the next soaking rain.
Cover sown spots lightly with mulch once seedlings show, and scare birds.

records.title: Stunted plants with purplish leaves
records.summary: Stunted plants with purplish leaves: likely hungry, acidic soil that holds back plant food
instructions: Check moisture and drainage first.
Work mature compost or rotted manure around the plants and mulch.
For the next sowing, add more organic matter and favour tolerant crops.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
likely_causes: Hungry, acidic soil that holds back plant food
Cold, dry or waterlogged roots
actions: Check moisture and drainage first.
Work mature compost or rotted manure around the plants and mulch.
For the next sowing, add more organic matter and favour tolerant crops.

records.title: Stunted, pale yellow plants
records.summary: Stunted, pale yellow plants: likely possible shortage of plant food
instructions: Check the soil a finger deep, drainage and pests first.
If those are fine, add a light top-up of mature compost around plants and watch for a week or two.
Grow legumes next to or after cereals.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
likely_causes: Possible shortage of plant food
Dry roots, waterlogging, pests or disease can look the same
actions: Check the soil a finger deep, drainage and pests first.

records.title: Leaves yellow between green veins
records.summary: Leaves yellow between green veins: likely too much ash, shell or other liming material added
instructions: Stop adding ash or shell.
Add mature compost and let the rains wash through.
Keep an untreated comparison pit.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.

records.summary: The baking-soda fizz seems unchanged after a trial: likely the fizz check is not a reliable measure and may not show any change
instructions: Do not keep adding ash to chase a change in fizz.
Judge by plant health against an untreated pit.
Seek local advice before adding more of anything.

instructions: Break the crust gently with a stick or fingertip after rain.
Mulch lightly around sown spots once seedlings show.
Mix more organic matter into the top of pits and beds next time.

Check the soil is damp a finger deep; water at the base only if it is dry.

records.title: Plants wilt and do not recover by morning

Thin crowded plants so fewer share the water.
Thicken mulch; check the stem base for termites or rot.

Remove dead wood near beds.
Keep seedlings moist; re-sow lost spots.
Seek local advice before disturbing a large mound.

records.summary: Sweet potato makes vines but few roots: likely bed or mound too shallow
instructions: Build taller, looser mounds next time.
Use only moderate compost.
Mulch, and pile soil over cracks.

Harvest promptly once grain is hard.

records.title: A small purple-flowered weed grows among millet
records.summary: A small purple-flowered weed grows among millet: likely striga (witchweed), a parasitic weed of cereals on poor soil
instructions: Pull it carefully by hand before it seeds; bag it and burn or bury it away from the plot.
Rotate with cowpea next season and feed the soil with compost.
limitations: Several causes can look alike; check the simple ones (water, drainage, pests) first.
